page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-72 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance built on the arm64 64-bit processor architecture. The configuration supplies 72 dedicated virtual cores paired with 288 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 4 GB of memory per core. The instance operates without discrete hardware acceleration, featuring zero graphics processing units.

Storage architecture relies entirely on external network-attached block storage volumes, as the instance includes no integrated local NVMe solid-state storage. Network connectivity provisions do not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating standard virtual private cloud routing, NAT gateways, or reserved external IP assignments for public network communication.

The arm64 core count and memory capacity offer qualitative cost-efficiency benefits through modern energy-efficient core density. Tradeoffs include the requirement for software compatibility with the 64-bit ARM instruction set and total reliance on remote persistent disks for persistence and scratch space. The resource profile aligns with large-scale multi-threaded workloads, enterprise web serving layers, continuous integration pipelines, microservices clusters, and general-purpose backend compute tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-72 is a general-purpose compute instance based on the 64-bit arm64 architecture. It provides 72 dedicated vCPUs and 288 GB of total system memory, preserving a standard resource distribution of 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance contains zero GPUs and features no onboard local storage, requiring network-attached persistent disks for operating system and data requirements. Without complimentary public IPv4 addresses, network egress and public access depend on standard cloud routing mechanisms. With its balanced memory ratio and high virtual core count, the arm64 architecture provides efficient resource density for concurrent application tiers. System administrators must account for ARM binary requirements and external volume storage latencies. The instance fits large multi-tier application deployments, parallel build pipelines, container clusters, data transformation jobs, and general business application hosting.
